'''Charles Gabriel Kurland''' (born 14 January 1936) is an American-born Swedish biochemist.

Kurland earned a doctorate in 1961 at [[Harvard University]], advised by [[James D. Watson]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Kurland, Charles, 1967 September 15-1974 May 22, 1967 September 15-1974 May 22 |url=https://hollisarchives.lib.harvard.edu/repositories/14/archival_objects/1912210 |access-date=10 March 2022 |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref><ref name="estoniagf">{{cite news |title=Charles G. Kurland |url=http://www.geneforum.ee/Kurland.pdf |access-date=10 March 2022 |publisher=Annual International Gene Forum |date=15 September 2001 |archive-date=17 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617185854/http://www.geneforum.ee/Kurland.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Kurland accepted a postdoctoral research position at the Microbiology Institute of the [[University of Copenhagen]], then joined the [[Uppsala University]] faculty in 1971.<ref name="estoniagf"/> He retired from Uppsala in 2001 and was granted emeritus status.<ref name="eeas">{{cite news |title=Charles Gabriel Kurland |url=https://www.akadeemia.ee/en/member/kurland/ |access-date=10 March 2022 |publisher=Estonian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He was later affiliated with [[Lund University]].<ref name="estoniagf"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Våra förfäder var glupska eukaryoter |url=https://www.forskning.se/2006/05/29/vara-forfader-varglupska-eukaryoter/ |access-date=10 March 2022 |work=Forskning |date=29 May 2006 |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Charles Kurland |url=https://portal.research.lu.se/en/persons/charles-kurland |access-date=10 March 2022 |publisher=Lund University}}</ref>

==Research==

Kurland's doctoral work dealt the structure of RNA,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/S0022-2836(60)80029-0
|volume = 1|number=  2|year = 1960| pages = 83–91
|journal=J. Mol. Biol. 
|title = Molecular characterization of ribonucleic acid from ''Escherichia coli'' ribosomes: I. Isolation and molecular weights
|first = C.G.|last = Kurland
}}</ref> and continued with the discovery of messenger RNA (mRNA), work that also involved [[François Gros]], [[Walter Gilbert]] and [[James Watson]].<ref>{{cite journal 
| doi= 10.1038/190581a0
| first1 = François | last1 = Gros
| first2 = H. | last2 = Hiatt
| first3 = Walter | last3 = Gilbert
| first4 = C. | last4 = Kurland
| first5 = R. W. | last5 = Risebrough
| first6 = J. D. | last6 = Watson
|title =Unstable ribonucleic acid revealed by pulse labelling of ''Escherichia coli''
|journal = Nature
|volume = 190|number = 4776| year = 1961| pages = 581–585
| bibcode = 1961Natur.190..581G }}</ref> This was published simultaneously with the report by [[Sydney Brenner]], [[François Jacob]], and [[Matthew Meselson]] of the same discovery.<ref> {{cite journal | doi= 10.1038/190576a0
| first1 = S. | last1 = Brenner
| first2 = F. | last2 =Jacob
| first3 =  M.| last3 =Meselson
|title =An unstable intermediate carrying information from genes to ribosomes for protein synthesis
|journal =Nature|volume = 190|number = 4776|year =  1961 | pages =  576–581| bibcode = 1961Natur.190..576B }}</ref> It was followed by numerous papers concerned with ribosomal proteins.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/bi00835a031
|title = Ribosomal proteins of ''Escherichia coli''. I. Purification of the 30 S ribosomal proteins
| first1 = S. J. S. | last1 = Hardy
| first2 = C. G. | last2 = Kurland
| first3 = P.  | last3 = Voynow
| first4 = G. | last4 = Mora
| journal = Biochemistry
| year = 1969|volume=8|number = 7| pages= 2897–2905
|pmid = 4897206
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal 
| doi= 10.1021/bi00835a032
| title = Ribosomal proteins of ''Escherichia coli''. II. Chemical and physical characterization of the 30 S ribosomal proteins
| first1 =R. | last1 = Gary
| first2 = P.  | last2 = Craven
| first3 = S. J. S. | last3 = Hardy
| first4 = C. G. | last4 = Kurland
| journal = Biochemistry 
| year = 1969|volume=8|number = 7| pages= 2906–2915
| pmid = 4897207
}}</ref>

In the later part of his career, Kurland has been interested in the origins of mitochondria<ref>{{cite journal 
| doi= 10.1016/j.jtbi.2017.07.011
|title = Mitochondria are not captive bacteria
|journal = J. Theor. Biol.
|first1 = Ajith | last1 = Harish
| first2 = C. G. | last2 = Kurland
|volume = 434|year = 2017| pages = 88–98
|pmid = 28754286
|bibcode = 2017JThBi.434...88H
}}</ref> and the tree of life.<ref>{{cite journal 
| doi= 10.1016/j.biochi.2017.04.013
|title = Akaryotes and Eukaryotes are independent descendants of a universal common ancestor
|journal = Biochimie
|first1 = Ajith | last1 = Harish
| first2 = C. G. | last2 = Kurland
|volume = 138|year = 2017| pages = 168–183
|pmid = 28461155
}}</ref>

==Academy memberships==
Kurland was elected to the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 1988 as a foreign member and reclassified as a Swedish member in 2002.<ref>{{cite news |title=Charles Kurland |url=https://www.kva.se/sv/om-oss/kontakt/charles-kurland |access-date=10 March 2022 |publisher=Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]] recognized his achievements in biochemistry and awarded Kurland an equivalent honor in 1991.<ref name="eeas"/>
